staple noun and verb

also staples, staple together

modern

Traupman 31: uncīnulus (metallicus)
Andresian p. 12

uncīnulus, uncīnulī m.

noun, second declension

a staple (for paper)

A little hook; a diminutive of late Latin uncīnus (Lewis & Short). Traupman adds metallicus where it needs saying.

Other words

  • cōnsuō, cōnsuere, cōnsuī, cōnsūtum — to staple, sew together

    verb, third conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 31; Varr. LL 9.79: tunicam (Lewis & Short)

    Classically to stitch together; Traupman’s verb for stapling papers.

See also stapler, paper.
